page: Amazon Web Services i2.2xlarge is a legacy generation storage-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 Ivy Bridge processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, supported by a 25 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 61.0 GB of RAM, equating to 7.62 GB per vCPU, with 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and no included public IPv4 addresses.

A central feature of the i2.2xlarge hardware configuration is its 1,600 GB of bundled local SSD storage, designed to deliver high internal disk throughput for transactional systems. The instance does not feature dedicated GPU acceleration. Benchmark results reflect the aging Ivy Bridge microarchitecture, yielding lower computational metrics on modern tests with a Geekbench single-core score of 529.0 and multi-core score of 2015.0. Stress-ng and PassMark CPU benchmarks place overall multi-core computational throughput within average boundaries, recording a PassMark CPU score of 8,839.65.

Data handling performance is marked by average database operation throughput and PassMark memory metrics, though memory write speeds and compression throughput lag behind modern platforms. Redis SET throughput achieves 3.05 million operations per second, while static web serving reaches 7.59 GB/sec. Given the older processor architecture and low network bandwidth relative to modern instances, cost efficiency is primarily realized through the high density of bundled local SSD storage and substantial RAM capacity rather than raw compute speed.

The i2.2xlarge is suited for legacy I/O-intensive workloads, transactional databases, intermediate NoSQL deployments, and data caching tiers that rely heavily on large local SSD capacity and memory rather than intensive CPU or vector processing.
description: Amazon Web Services i2.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the Xen hypervisor, it provides 61.0 GB of system memory, alongside a bundled 1,600 GB local SSD storage array and a 1 Gbps baseline network link. The platform lacks GPU acceleration and modern vector instruction sets like AVX-512, which reflects in lower single-core Geekbench scores, though multi-core compute throughput remains stable on standard stress tests. Its primary strength lies in high-capacity local disk storage paired with substantial memory density, accommodating workloads such as legacy transactional databases, NoSQL data nodes, and read-heavy caching systems.
